From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
"Deacon Jones Award" redirects here. For the Black college award, see Deacon Jones Trophy.
Myles Garrett holds the official single-season record for sacks with 23.
This is a list of National Football League (NFL) players who have led the regular season in sacks each year. Sacks became an official statistic in 1982 and sacks from years prior do not count towards a player's career total.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_NFL_annual_sacks_leaders#cite_note-1)Myles Garrett of the Los Angeles Rams holds the official record with 23, set during the 2025 season.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_NFL_annual_sacks_leaders#cite_note-2)
The **Deacon Jones Award** was established by the NFL in 2013 to recognize the annual leader in sacks, named after the former defensive end Deacon Jones who led the league in sacks five times.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_NFL_annual_sacks_leaders#cite_note-3) Since 1982, there have only been two players who have led the league in sacks with two different teams, Jared Allen (2007 with the Chiefs and 2011 with the Vikings) and Kevin Greene (1994 with the Steelers and 1996 with the Panthers). The Chiefs and the Vikings have had the most players lead the NFL in sacks with four. Seven players have been the league leader in sacks twice, while T. J. Watt has led the league three times.

## NFL annual sacks leaders
[edit]
Jared Allen led the league in sacks in 2007 and 2011.
Al Baker is the unofficial NFL record holder with 23 sacks during the 1978 NFL season.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_NFL_annual_sacks_leaders#cite_note-SingleSeasonLeaders-4)
The Deacon Jones Award, given annually to the player who leads the league in sacks, is named after Deacon Jones. Jones unofficially led the league in sacks five times.
_Note that the sack totals from 1960 to 1981 are considered unofficial by the NFL_.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_NFL_annual_sacks_leaders#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_NFL_annual_sacks_leaders#cite_note-6)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
"Deacon Jones Award" redirects here. For the Black college award, see Deacon Jones Trophy.
Myles Garrett holds the official single-season record for sacks with 23.
This is a list of National Football League (NFL) players who have led the regular season in sacks each year. Sacks became an official statistic in 1982 and sacks from years prior do not count towards a player's career total.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_NFL_annual_sacks_leaders#cite_note-1)Myles Garrett of the Los Angeles Rams holds the official record with 23, set during the 2025 season.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_NFL_annual_sacks_leaders#cite_note-2)
The **Deacon Jones Award** was established by the NFL in 2013 to recognize the annual leader in sacks, named after the former defensive end Deacon Jones who led the league in sacks five times.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_NFL_annual_sacks_leaders#cite_note-3) Since 1982, there have only been two players who have led the league in sacks with two different teams, Jared Allen (2007 with the Chiefs and 2011 with the Vikings) and Kevin Greene (1994 with the Steelers and 1996 with the Panthers). The Chiefs and the Vikings have had the most players lead the NFL in sacks with four. Seven players have been the league leader in sacks twice, while T. J. Watt has led the league three times.

Myles Garrett holds the official single-season record for sacks with 23.
This is a list of National Football League (NFL) players who have led the regular season in sacks each year. Sacks became an official statistic in 1982 and sacks from years prior do not count towards a player's career total.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_NFL_annual_sacks_leaders#cite_note-1)Myles Garrett of the Los Angeles Rams holds the official record with 23, set during the 2025 season.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_NFL_annual_sacks_leaders#cite_note-2)
The **Deacon Jones Award** was established by the NFL in 2013 to recognize the annual leader in sacks, named after the former defensive end Deacon Jones who led the league in sacks five times.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_NFL_annual_sacks_leaders#cite_note-3) Since 1982, there have only been two players who have led the league in sacks with two different teams, Jared Allen (2007 with the Chiefs and 2011 with the Vikings) and Kevin Greene (1994 with the Steelers and 1996 with the Panthers). The Chiefs and the Vikings have had the most players lead the NFL in sacks with four. Seven players have been the league leader in sacks twice, while T. J. Watt has led the league three times.

## NFL annual sacks leaders
[edit]
Jared Allen led the league in sacks in 2007 and 2011.
Al Baker is the unofficial NFL record holder with 23 sacks during the 1978 NFL season.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_NFL_annual_sacks_leaders#cite_note-SingleSeasonLeaders-4)
The Deacon Jones Award, given annually to the player who leads the league in sacks, is named after Deacon Jones. Jones unofficially led the league in sacks five times.
_Note that the sack totals from 1960 to 1981 are considered unofficial by the NFL_.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_NFL_annual_sacks_leaders#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_NFL_annual_sacks_leaders#cite_note-6)
